Wednesday, May 20, 2020  6:00 PM  Teleconference

Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, General Plan Advisory Committee Members will be
participating via teleconference.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
823 6068 8991, Password: 278686. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 823 6068 8991, Password: 278686.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MAY 20, 2020

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Addleman, Bayer, Buresh, Corman,
  Friedman, Seamans, Shinn, Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Arata, Carman, Carrese, Medawar, Silvano,
  Stegura

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  Aaron Lobliner, Planner, Michael Baker International
  Veronica Tam, Veronica Tam and Associates, Inc.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  APRIL 29, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
ADDLEMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  APRIL 29, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  SAFETY ELEMENT POLICIES
John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International (MBI), introduced Veronica Tam, who will be
introducing the Housing Element.

Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, MBI, led the discussion on the topics to be reviewed.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policies:

  •  New Policy: Reduce the risk of wildfire hazards by working with Homeowner Associations,
  Business Park Associations, property owners, and the Los Angeles County Fire
  Department (LACFD) to maintain fire-retardant landscaping and buffer zones in areas of
  high wildfire risk.

  •  New Policy: Encourage all new development to incorporate fire-safe design, including
  sufficient ingress/egress, evacuation routes, emergency vehicle access, visible home
  addressing and signage, and fuel modification zones.
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, MAY 20, 2020
   •  New Policy: Encourage property owners to provide defensible space in between
  vegetation and structures, as outlined by the Los Angeles County Fire Department.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER and COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN stated that it is
important to include brush abatement.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN stated that “fuel modified” may be confusing to people, and
suggested using “fire-retardant” instead.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that “property owner” is mentioned in the first and
third policy in a similar way.

Ms. Barbhaya stated the changes are noted and the policies will be revised.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that the ideas to get across are that there are standards enforced by Los
Angeles County Fire Department; and, when people build, that they are encouraged to have fuel
modifications in mind.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policies:

  •  New Policy: Update and maintain the City's Emergency Operations Plan, which provides
  procedures for responding to disasters, including emergency ingress and egress, and
  defines the expected roles of City, County, and regional agencies.

  •  New Policy: Identify rights-of-way that do not provide adequate clearance for emergency
  vehicles; for areas not accessible, develop a contingency plan for reaching and evacuating
  people in need of treatment.

  •  New Policy: Work with Los Angeles County and neighboring jurisdictions to catalog
  roadways that can serve as evacuation routes from the Palos Verdes Peninsula in case
  of emergencies.

  •  New Policy: Provide for an expedited permit approval process following a major disaster
  to bolster allowable reconstruction efforts.

  •  New Policy: Coordinate with the citizen groups and organizations on the Peninsula to
  identify a viable body to provide emergency assistance in the event of a disaster or health
  crisis.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHMITZ, Administrative Analyst Slawson confirmed that
the language in these policies is consistent with that found in the Joint Hazard Mitigation Plan.

After a brief discussion, there were no changes to the policies presented.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policy:

  •  New Policy: Provide information and participate in applicable in local, regional, state, and
  federal programs that educate residents and businesses about how to protect themselves
  and their property from hazards, public health crises, and climate change.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that this policy is too detailed for a general plan.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested the following change:

  •  Provide information and participate in applicable appropriate in local, regional, state, and
  federal programs that educate residents and businesses about how to protect themselves
  and their property from hazards, public health crises, and climate change.”

After a brief discussion, the committee agreed that this policy be reworded to be more generalized.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, MAY 20, 2020
 Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policy:

  •  New Policy: Work with local, state, and federal agencies to update, monitor, and maintain
  the most current flood hazard and floodplain information.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER stated that this policy is too detailed.

After a brief discussion, Ms. Barbhaya stated that this policy will be simplified and may be moved
from a policy to an implementation strategy.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policy:

  •  New Policy: Support slope mitigation on potentially unstable hillside areas, especially
  slopes with recurring failures or where City property/public right-of-way is threatened.
  •  New Policy: Require erosion prevention of hillside areas by revegetation or other
  acceptable measures.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BURESH expressed her concern with using the word “support” since it
is not used in any other policy and may suggest a monetary obligation.

After a brief discussion, the committee agreed to change these policies as follows:

  •  Support Encourage slope mitigation on potentially unstable hillside areas, especially
  slopes with recurring failures or where City property/public right-of-way is threatened.

  •  Require erosion prevention plans of hillside areas by revegetation or other acceptable
  measures.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policies:

  •  Existing Policy: Ensure that no hazardous materials are dumped in Chandler Quarry
  landfill or in any other areas of the City.

  •  Revised Policy: Ensure that no hazardous materials are dumped in any areas of the City.

  •  Existing Policy: Work to promote the safe use and disposal of household hazardous
  wastes.

  •  Revised Policy: Encourage the community to safely dispose of toxic substances,
  household hazardous waste, electronic waste, and other hazardous materials through
  established Waste Collection partnerships.

After a brief discussion, there were no changes to these policies.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policies:

  •  New Policy: Promote after school programs, citizen volunteer programs, and
  neighborhood watch programs to help maintain a safe environment.

  •  New Policy: Apply Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) principles
  to new development projects, major renovations, and public projects.

  •  New Policy: Ensure that adequate To the extent possible, provide adequate street and
  property lighting is provided to discourage crime while preventing unnecessary light
  pollution or spillover.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 MINUTES, MAY 20, 2020
 After a brief discussion, the third policy will be removed and the second policy will be changed as
follows:
  • New Policy: Apply Encourage Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED)
  principles to new development projects, major renovations, and public projects.

Ms. Barbhaya presented the following policies:

  •  New Policy: Update the City's Climate Action Plan on a regular basis, including those
  strategies that consider the unique characteristics and conditions of the City.

  •  New Policy: Continue to support the preservation of natural systems throughout the City,
  such as natural drainage features and wetlands/riparian areas, that provide resilience to
  hazards that could be exacerbated by climate change, as suggested in Conservation
  Element as well as Open Space and Recreation Element.

  •  New Policy: Designate public buildings, specific private buildings, or institutions with air
  conditioning as public cooling shelters during periods of extreme heat or power outage.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that Sustainability Element be added to the second
policy.

There were no other changes.

B.  HOUSING ELEMENT
Veronica Tam, Veronica Tam and Associates, Inc., provided a presentation on the Housing
Element, which is one of the eight required elements of the general plan.
Ms. Tam stated that the Housing Element differs from the general plan in many ways.
Per the Government Code on General Plan regulations, jurisdictions are required to include the
following:

  •  Provide a variety of housing types of all income groups
  •  Assist in the development of lower and moderate income housing
  •  Remove constraints to housing
  •  Conserve and improve existing housing
  •  Promote fair housing
Ms. Tam provided information on the Housing Element update process, including:

  •  The deadline for the Housing Element Update for the Southern California region – October
  15, 2021 with a 120-day grace period.
  •  Mandatory review by the State Department of Housing and Community Development
  (HCD) for compliance with State law – Draft and Final Review
Ms. Tam explained the consequences for non-compliance.
Ms. Tam provided an overview of the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA), which is a key
component of the HCD review. This included the RHNA number for Rolling Hills Estates, which
is estimated at 191. She further explained the RHNA income distribution rate and household
income distribution, including income groups and how they are categorized.
Ms. Tam provided an overview on recent legislation in regards to affordable housing, which
includes removing development constraints and expanding housing options.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired if the AMI (area median income) is based on
County or State income limits. Ms. Tam responded that it is based on County income limit.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked about Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) qualifying
to meet income levels if they are rental units. Ms. Tam stated that ADUs only qualify once they
are built and in order to allocate that into income levels, it has to be based on actual rents.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  4
 MINUTES, MAY 20, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN asked if the city gets affordable housing credit for assisted
living facilities. Ms. Tam stated that assisted living developments are comprised of different types
of housing - from independent living to nursing care. Most of the time, you would not receive credit
for it because developers will typically pull permits for one commercial development. However,
she stated that she has recommended to her clients that when an application comes in for an
assisted living development, try to work with the developer to separate permits for those units that
qualify as residential.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Tam stated that a
rooming house itself may qualify as one unit.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER, Ms. Tam stated that residential
nursing homes do not typically qualify.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if the information on how these numbers are going
to be met in respect to geographical locations is going to be found in Land Use or in the Housing
Element. Director Wahba stated that this will be found and discussed in the Land Use Element
and Housing Element.

Mr. Bellas stated that this is an introduction to the Housing Element; however, the Land Use
Element is next to be discussed since it will tie in with the Housing Element.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that the next two meetings will focus on the Land Use Element. One meeting
could be used to identify sites and figure out land use. After the two meetings, the focus will be
on the commercial district.

Ms. Tam stated that the goal would be for the draft Housing Element be prepared by late Fall.

A brief discussion was held regarding the future meeting dates. Staff will poll the committee for
the next June meeting date(s).

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Tam stated that 30-35% of
total income would be the typical rent to be considered affordable housing, but this information
could be found in the health and safety code.

6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS

NONE

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:56 p.m.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  5
 MINUTES, MAY 20, 2020
